[Issue #9904] Dual-validate URLs in CG transformation to fix search 500 (#9911)

## Summary

Fixes #9904.

`POST /common-grants/opportunities/search` was 500ing when the result
page contained a URL that pydantic accepts but marshmallow rejects (most
often comma-separated URLs from grants.gov data). The CG response is
loaded back through marshmallow on the way out, so one bad record killed
the whole batch. Fix validates URLs against both libraries at the
transformation source so divergent strings get dropped instead of
crashing the response.

## Changes proposed

- New `api/src/services/common_grants/url_utils.py` with
`validate_url_compatible` — a dual-validator that requires both pydantic
`HttpUrl` (strict) and marshmallow `fields.URL` to accept the input,
returning the pydantic-normalized form so the exact string downstream
callers see is the one the response load re-validates.
- `validate_url` and `AttachmentValue.validate_download_url` both
delegate to the new helper. Removed `UrlValidator` and
`_AttachmentUrlValidator` (consolidated onto one strict-mode pydantic
validator). Introduced a single module-level `_marshmallow_url_field`
singleton in `url_utils.py` for the dual-validation path.
- URL-validation log: fixed message string at WARNING severity; URL plus
field path and `opportunity_id` in `extra` (so operators can answer "why
is this field missing for opportunity X?" without paging the source
record).
- Tests: `test_url_utils.py` (6 unit tests for `validate_url_compatible`
covering both divergent cases — comma-separated URLs and
scheme-only-host) and additions to `test_transformation.py`
(divergent-URL rejection at `validate_url`, end-to-end reproduction
through `OpportunitiesSearchResponseSchema().load(...)`, the attachment
sibling case, and a guard that the drop-log carries `field` +
`opportunity_id`).

## Context for reviewers

Prod traceback (from #9904):
```
ValidationError({'items': {0: {'customFields': {'additionalInfo': {'value':
{'url': [...message='Not a valid URL.']}}}}}})
```
Stack pointed at
`OpportunitiesSearchResponseSchema().load(response_json)` in
[common_grants_routes.py:173](api/src/api/common_grants/common_grants_routes.py#L173).

Confirmed divergent inputs (pydantic accepts, marshmallow rejects):
- `https://a.gov,https://b.gov` — pydantic mangles to
`https://a.gov,https//b.gov`
- `http://example` — pydantic accepts TLD-less hosts

Two behavior changes worth flagging:
- `AttachmentValue.downloadUrl` now stores the pydantic-normalized form
(trailing slash, lowercase host) instead of raw input — matches what
`validate_url` has done since #6987.
- Attachment URLs now run through strict-mode pydantic. The deleted
`_AttachmentUrlValidator` was non-strict; the marshmallow load already
rejected curly-brace URLs etc., this just moves the rejection earlier.

Suggested follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Lock the marshmallow side to `http`/`https` (the dual-check already
restricts to those via pydantic strict `HttpUrl`, but defense-in-depth
is cheap).
- Surface a `dataWarnings` envelope so consumers can see suppressed
fields.
- Apply per-record fail-soft to v1 `search_opportunities`
`SCHEMA.load(many=True)` for the same atomic-batch brittleness.

## Validation steps

```bash
make test args="tests/src/services/common_grants -v"
```
Suite covers the dual-validator unit cases and the prod-failing
reproduction through the marshmallow response load.

After deploy, confirm the prod-failing payload returns 200:
```bash
curl -X POST 'https://api.simpler.grants.gov/common-grants/opportunities/search' \
  -H 'X-API-Key: <KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"filters":{"status":{"operator":"in","value":["closed"]}},"pagination":{"page":22,"pageSize":1},"search":"open data"}'
```
Expect 200, a WARNING log with `cg_event=url_validation_error`, the URL,
the field path, and the `opportunity_id`, and the New Relic "API Prod -
Error Logs" alert to clear.

head_commit.message:
Restore DMS networking module in separate file

The nava-platform CLI regenerates infra/networks/main.tf from a template,
which caused the DMS networking module to be removed during the v0.15.7 update.

Created infra/networks/dms.tf to hold the DMS networking configuration separately.
This file won't be touched by template updates, preserving the DMS module across
future template-infra upgrades.

[Issue #9904] Drop URL userinfo redaction; log raw URL on validation failure

These URLs are public — grants.gov and SGG already serve them unredacted.
Hand-rolled sanitization in the logging path adds bug surface (the lazy
ValueError on SplitResult.port was the canary) without protecting anything
that wasn't already public. If we ever do want logger-level URL scrubbing,
that belongs in a separate PR at the logger or service layer where it can
apply uniformly.

Removes redact_url_userinfo and its tests; validate_url now logs the raw
URL in extra["url"]. Also drops the stale TODO(@widal001) comment that
got carried over from the original transformation.py validator.

head_commit.message:
[Issue #9904] Log dropped-URL events with field path and opportunity_id (WARNING)

Per review feedback on PR #9911: when validate_url drops a URL the field is
silently omitted from the CG response, leaving operators with no way to
answer 'why is this field missing for opportunity X?' when an API consumer
asks. Address the troubleshooting half of that gap by enriching the log:

- validate_url(value, *, field=None, opportunity_id=None) — both threaded
  into extra so log queries can filter by either.
- Bumped INFO -> WARNING. Suppressing a field on the consumer-facing
  response is a data-quality event, not a routine validation observation.
- Message changed from 'URL validation failed' to 'Dropping URL field
  from CG response: failed dual validation' so it's self-describing in
  log aggregation.
- Threaded field/opportunity_id through three callsites in transformation.py
  (source, customFields.additionalInfo.url, customFields.attachments[].
  downloadUrl). Attachment path now pre-validates before AttachmentValue
  construction so the drop is observable in the same WARNING; the pydantic
  field validator stays as a defensive backstop.
- Added test asserting all three field paths land in WARNING records with
  opportunity_id attached.

Bigger lift (a 'dataWarnings' envelope on the response so API consumers
can self-diagnose suppressed fields without log access) deliberately
deferred — that one warrants team alignment and probably an ADR.

Code review surfaced a bug: SplitResult.port lazily raises ValueError on
non-numeric ports (e.g. 'host:abc'). The old try only wrapped urlsplit(),
so port access on a malformed URL would propagate, crashing the log call
and re-introducing the fail-hard 500 this module exists to prevent.

Fix: move parse + reconstruct entirely inside the try, catch ValueError on
both urlsplit() and the lazy port access, return the unparseable sentinel.

Adds test_url_utils.py with focused tests on redact_url_userinfo (incl. the
malformed-port regression guard) and validate_url_compatible. Also carries
the SDK-strictness TODO from the deleted UrlValidator class.

[Issue #9904] Extract dual URL validation to url_utils + redact userinfo on log

Self-review (3 parallel reviewers) flagged three Majors:
- simplicity: validate_download_url duplicated the dual-validate logic from
  validate_url; two _marshmallow_url_field singletons.
- correctness: validate_download_url passed raw v to marshmallow while
  validate_url passed pydantic-normalized — fragile asymmetry.
- security: validate_url logged the raw URL (potential user:password@) in
  both message body and extra. PII filter doesn't strip URL credentials.

Fix:
- New api/src/services/common_grants/url_utils.py exposing
  validate_url_compatible(value) — single source of truth that normalizes via
  pydantic then validates the normalized form against marshmallow.
- Both validate_url (transformation.py) and AttachmentValue.validate_download_url
  (custom_fields.py) delegate to it. _AttachmentUrlValidator class deleted.
- redact_url_userinfo(value) strips user:password@ before logging. Log message
  is now a fixed string; URL only in extra['url'].
- New test asserts credentials don't leak through either log surface.
